subject.title: fix(sessions): enforce exact owner equality for all parent session use and narrow catch

question: Should plugin runtimes fail closed on legacy ownerless session rows across create, parent use, reset, patch, and delete, or must an operator migration path precede enforcement?
rationale: The strict behavior improves isolation but intentionally breaks any existing plugin workflow that adopted ownerless rows; tests cannot determine the repository's compatibility policy.

options.title: Fail Closed Consistently
options.body: Reject ownerless rows across every plugin-runtime session operation, document the upgrade impact, and use one shared authorization policy.

options.title: Migrate Before Enforcement
options.body: Add a doctor or explicit operator-owned migration that assigns or retires legacy ownerless rows before enabling the strict boundary.

recommendation.title: Fail Closed Consistently
recommendation.body: Reject ownerless rows across every plugin-runtime session operation, document the upgrade impact, and use one shared authorization policy.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent parent-session work and the existing PR discussion make this person the closest available routing candidate for the session ownership policy.
